doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Editing artists he does not love, such as Joe Zawinul
summary: He says personal taste affects Grove articles little, since they focus on biographical and discographical facts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Well I don’t have to ask that question now. Sometimes I do ask that question, of time travel, but you just took care of it already. So in your role as an editor you’ve done so much of it. I wonder if it’s sometimes hard for you if there’s an artist that really demands attention and of course should be included whether it’s the book or the on-line edition, but you don’t particularly care for their music. Do you recognize that you might need to hand this off to somebody else or does it affect the way you think about including them?

I like to think that it would affect it only in a small way. There are things like that, it does happen. If I can hand it off I will, sure I’d be happy to have someone do it who is a complete enthusiast for it. But I think that is much less of a problem for Grove, where we’re so concerned with the nitty gritty biographical and discographical and videographical details and bibliographical details, and not with say writing a book about them or writing a review of their record, which is a different kind of writing that I wouldn’t dream of taking on if I wasn’t the favorite. All right, here’s an example. Joe Zawinul — well I’m sorry, except for “Birdland” he just bores me to tears. He’s not a favorite. I have huge, wide-ranging loves in jazz. I have really eclectic taste. It’s a great thing for Grove because there’s so much stuff I like. But sometimes, yes, you’re exactly right, there’s somebody that just bores me. But I don’t think that that handicaps very much writing a Zawinul Grove article. It’s pretty clear how important he was, what he did, and why he was important, and that’s what we want to see in a Grove article.
